dialogue.speaker: 096309C246D4D66751C4A5B5917FFFEE
dialogue.line: Knyaz Catalin will probably help a bit, I reckon. But he's got quite a lot to do.

dialogue.speaker: 7D967AEC4BF65DE0940F26ACA2CB397E
dialogue.line: Look – people of Laslea are a resourceful lot. But this winter will be harsh on everyone...

dialogue.speaker: 0CFF32E442F75C9767208CB9C9F056DE
dialogue.line: Might have just the thing. Let me check on my cart.

dialogue.speaker: 462934F1458BEAA640EE66B94153D9B2
dialogue.line: Of course, of course. I imagine you're very busy, being a hero and all.

dialogue.speaker: AFC9DA1A4D66D6FAC959F9B07F78B652
dialogue.line: Oh, shit. No, no, Coen – didn't mean that, of course. Just pointing out the challenges.

dialogue.speaker: A3B8033A455E5A6A7A1FF09B70B558AB
dialogue.line: Really? If you don't mind - go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: EB5C4C37481FB96CDB959EAA71112DEE
dialogue.line: Seriously? You'd prefer them?

dialogue.speaker: 2C2C72A84F11ED07956925B72E75C87B
dialogue.line: Seriously? You'd prefer those monsters had stayed in power?

dialogue.speaker: 81500CDE4F5A21EDE58D6CA49E3693C8
dialogue.line: Shit...

dialogue.speaker: 9E3D97A14372F267AD44DF8B01D0D2AC
dialogue.line: Some will squabble over the throne... and some will use this as a chance to make a profit, even on the misery of other wretches.

dialogue.speaker: 839B00FB4BCABD16F0027AAA6ECF269C
dialogue.line: Sorry to hear that. I'll just take that blanket and be out of your hair.

dialogue.speaker: 0DEE23F34717703B50BA63A929BCE6DB
dialogue.line: Speaking of – the blasted thing won't move. Can you believe it?

dialogue.speaker: F7AEF1504B51F77A7A9DEE85DC0FC631
dialogue.line: Thank you! Got to help one another, right? God knows Laslea will need more of that attitude in the near future.

dialogue.speaker: 5036E2F443AE82B1FCF87285CEDD7C79
dialogue.line: That should do it. Just make sure to take care of those other things - or you'll be stuck again in no time.

dialogue.speaker: 977D5C274A6C058DB543A58AA925F793
dialogue.line: That's human nature for you, my friend.

dialogue.speaker: 034ADEC247077CDF12B0F98D36B28A9F
dialogue.line: The deal you have with the knyaz? All well and good – not having to give up blood, no one getting their head chopped off when the lord is pissed off.

dialogue.speaker: BCB43D9D46833F41E5EB49A9043ABE06
dialogue.line: Well, the way I see it... Laslea is on its own.

dialogue.speaker: 44656B884FE58096D0C640ADDD12BE70
dialogue.line: What do you mean by that?

dialogue.speaker: 630C95DC414A7DACBBAB5CB62E7F964F
dialogue.line: What do you mean by that?

dialogue.speaker: 49405534430ACB3F122A219895A8D873
dialogue.line: Without Brencis, who knows what's going to happen? One thing's for sure – some folk will get silly ideas into their heads!

dialogue.speaker: A9C6FBF2487204B0DBB93382387771E4
dialogue.line: You might be right.

dialogue.speaker: B9186EEC439ABF7DCAA9A0BD7E3322B6
dialogue.line: You might be right. We've forgotten some of life's hardships.

dialogue.speaker: DE389A07469311CB0AD5FFB0FDA19EFA
dialogue.line: You too, Coen. You too.

dialogue.speaker: 249FF1524B1C24BC8E4576B9DF07A32D
dialogue.line: Ah, I won't tell you what to do, son. You asked and I gave you my answer.

dialogue.speaker: 532E07624DAC52CDD8D17691720B1778
dialogue.line: And I have problems of my own. The way things are now, I'm not even sure if my little lad will survive this winter.

dialogue.speaker: 97BD53ED4A4FC4AACAA595AF7BA9A69F
dialogue.line: And I remember what you did for me. The pig you brought back? My boy is still with us because I could give him a proper meal, help him regain his strength.

dialogue.speaker: 48B1748E4E544A4EE824B7888497AAA4
dialogue.line: Coen. You need anything? I'm busy.

dialogue.speaker: 367130CC423E9A02F7C76A8CECA53E8C
dialogue.line: Come on, Iorgu.

dialogue.speaker: 6E122EA14131432781E91A8B941DBBF8
dialogue.line: Don't you dare threaten me.

dialogue.speaker: 99C9B5E545B051E13568D28D24B1D678
dialogue.line: Don't you dare threaten me.

dialogue.speaker: 1269028148C42CE133070B98D1F26566
dialogue.line: Goodbye, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 9AC4EBDC48E456299625539BF07B6D72
dialogue.line: Hey, Iorgu.

dialogue.speaker: C6789A964D3196D75A9711A31510C5E8
dialogue.line: I appreciate the advice. But I will do what I want.

dialogue.speaker: E1D351B14AAF96DD6279C9907B50F8A0
dialogue.line: I might do just that.

dialogue.speaker: AB43AFE4411BEACE5D4CD6A9D803EBA7
dialogue.line: I might do just that. But first, I've got to take care of a few things.

dialogue.speaker: BF8BAE404BACAD7F9F672CA89497AB7C
dialogue.line: I wasn't trying to. Don't like my advice, don't take it.

dialogue.speaker: 714FBFC64F945FA93A3F258D77F2F352
dialogue.line: I'll do what I want.

dialogue.speaker: 58D2973B45D080D695C133BA19985B04
dialogue.line: I'll leave you be, then.

dialogue.speaker: 17DC95074190FE2E92DFC88D5F4222E7
dialogue.line: I'll leave you be.

dialogue.speaker: C9AF952046536A98E398A09CA8BCB694
dialogue.line: I'm busy, that's all.

dialogue.speaker: 397EE11A455F5ABEE3A43B8789CDE4BE
dialogue.line: I'm glad to hear that.

dialogue.speaker: 68F1EDB5478A1A9E8557468AC44FE054
dialogue.line: I'm sorry, Iorgu. Is there anything –

dialogue.speaker: 0CE4F8D0480A8CE4D7C41B8222FECC01
dialogue.line: Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: 13CD40F84740F2A7ACAF98B4890D6F4C
dialogue.line: Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: 9EF418BE4B155BE46F9518947AAE6C0D
dialogue.line: It's true, I am different.

dialogue.speaker: 5BD0C70F4B923CCE63EBE8BFD06C1C86
dialogue.line: It's true. But I swear you're not in any danger.

dialogue.speaker: 876BD0B74F51EAAA46E3FCAD8462D0DA
dialogue.line: Listen... I've already told you that I'll keep it to myself.

dialogue.speaker: E3ABABC2408619D355F40C9B3C8A6221
dialogue.line: Look, it's not my business. And I'm not going to say anything to anyone.

dialogue.speaker: 9DE61D924BDEA89EA91998AEF873B486
dialogue.line: Now, please, let me be. I have other things to worry about.

dialogue.speaker: B7C86FC14AFDE44920295D8685894EB7
dialogue.line: People see you as a hero now. But folks forget easily.

dialogue.speaker: 9CE32ED54D591200A239BDB87EB0D0E9
dialogue.line: Say anything about what?

dialogue.speaker: 5838E8E243FED3BFE55D208D0471E9B2
dialogue.line: Says you.

dialogue.speaker: CE5AFF81435DF5F846E99CA68B7A7FF8
dialogue.line: The animals... they behave differently when you're around. They're scared. And frankly, so am I.

dialogue.speaker: B9BAD59543B1349D3C73CCA06907A6DC
dialogue.line: You're imagining things.

dialogue.speaker: EEE8D594457F3F3769CAFF9FA5CD82C5
dialogue.line: You've... changed. You're not the lad I used to know. Not sure what is it, but... but I can tell, alright?

dialogue.speaker: 96815B304FB0303C2EFB039F3D2A89C8
dialogue.line: [scoff] You're imagining things.

dialogue.speaker: 661C20E64B288EA0AB9CD1A88F129312
dialogue.line: [sigh]

dialogue.speaker: A052151E4EFAD9A37CF07EAD2803E005
dialogue.line: [sighs] Leave, Coen. Before someone makes you.

dialogue.speaker: D91F1B2A4F10D9E224002781AAC9C468
dialogue.line: Ah. She probably thinks you should let your people take care of business. So, what will you do?

dialogue.speaker: 907FCC2C4460A354DB2BD3AB2B5257F6
dialogue.line: All uriash do. Vrakhiri dead, Brencis rule ended – we return mountains.

dialogue.speaker: EA1A85084BE80B0997CB48A9F65C04A9
dialogue.line: Always remember friend Coen! Bye!

dialogue.speaker: 2533B8CC4A692CB335220680E1E0CA42
dialogue.line: And how's Nora?

dialogue.speaker: 5C923ADC4165D44EDCC5209412410FE4
dialogue.line: And how's Nora?

dialogue.speaker: 6A726B774D7E790889FA0B86D91B65C5
dialogue.line: And what about your mother? Is she alright?

dialogue.speaker: F19BB5CE404E1C8BCA0C8EAB0CEC6359
dialogue.line: And your mother?

dialogue.speaker: 993415124A040107707899B2FED7C3A1
dialogue.line: Angry.

dialogue.speaker: B164B2E647560289F8CAE9A54C5E55BD
dialogue.line: Angry? What about?

dialogue.speaker: 0A4CCC564EDBDBC2C4957D82151B80B1
dialogue.line: Before I Elder, I go and visit all clan sacred place. One is near here.

dialogue.speaker: 5AB9CFE54B53D5EC4874F3AA652E8172
dialogue.line: But my choice. No look back.

dialogue.speaker: 5A2F7E6B4466418C6178A9BA397F0102
dialogue.line: Can't say. I really don't know what the future holds.

dialogue.speaker: 59B46B7C4E9DABF34AA59EB1F2E39AF7
dialogue.line: Do you miss home?

dialogue.speaker: 773C0F414A9B54E4329F3C9689214A64
dialogue.line: Farewell, Ocha.

dialogue.speaker: CA735DF0404F7FF2CFBDCB9A9ADC3F54
dialogue.line: Farewell, Ocha.

dialogue.speaker: D6B934B946D0AFF163779082AFB2B59A
dialogue.line: Good! I make... im-pre-ssion, yes?

dialogue.speaker: F4F187EB4EFABF0FF42032943ADF4A8A
dialogue.line: Goodbye? What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: FC8C177E41447C20475168961F91651A
dialogue.line: Ha! True! But now... many responsible.

dialogue.speaker: B02F290B47F8792432BB50963B9E30AE
dialogue.line: Hear Coen in Luhs-ley-ah. Decide to come and see!

dialogue.speaker: 220B69084B530A4AFE6EC1A0E6E5F30E
dialogue.line: Hm. City home now.

dialogue.speaker: A9A010FE42360038E51CDC9182093021
dialogue.line: I understand.

dialogue.speaker: 62E8912343737E27226BF69317D94D8B
dialogue.line: I understand. Thank you for finding the time to visit me, then.

dialogue.speaker: 433C714046FE9650F3F646B3AABEE1BF
dialogue.line: I'll miss you, Ocha.

dialogue.speaker: 1B2B1EBE4BFA4762FBC88DBB291153A2
dialogue.line: I'm glad it worked out, in the end.

dialogue.speaker: 65D50D7B415E98DE4B61E7A8710E5A7B
dialogue.line: I'm glad it worked out.

dialogue.speaker: 347C771243C32EC5F071D09C29DEE50A
dialogue.line: Is fine. We wait and see, right?

dialogue.speaker: 4FB7E931499F7F296DDD3EA20CBEC50F
dialogue.line: Is on way, no problem.

dialogue.speaker: 3748C8044405AA82E0CD40A638C53BEE
dialogue.line: I’ll miss you, Ocha.

dialogue.speaker: 169814784CDD3ECEB8E0A7B50F1C9263
dialogue.line: Listen. Hah! Argue with Nora – stupid.

dialogue.speaker: 0EB040C74FFC5CF06FF4DC8D8FCCC8A6
dialogue.line: No problems, then? You simply took over Andrei's business and contacts?

dialogue.speaker: 4CD0D56146B1FE8D6E400CB9BF533FBC
dialogue.line: Now, Brencis dead. Vrakhiri no rule, so uriash return mountain. But I stay in city. Hide.

dialogue.speaker: 257B1EA9485E833DADDFBDA3788BCF87
dialogue.line: Ocha! What the hell are you doing here?

dialogue.speaker: E9C4653D4AD20337A661DD84B9084D10
dialogue.line: Oh, I'm glad that you did, but is everything alright?

dialogue.speaker: 73334373434B075960ED1DB6B879599B
dialogue.line: Oh, some problem. But I smart. And fair. People see I more good than Andrei!

dialogue.speaker: 2D096A6A4B660CF53C750193E618B208
dialogue.line: On the way? To what?

dialogue.speaker: 9A4C23874254E7AE94267290F6B3F58B
dialogue.line: She fine. But she old, become weak. Clan re-spect, but clan need strong lead.

dialogue.speaker: 437F8557439F6D4C00A0DE824AE76171
dialogue.line: She say I do too many. She say I too... What word? Hmmm. Im-por-tant!

dialogue.speaker: 73876B4B4FAED7234B5A609C2E9033C6
dialogue.line: Sure, but what about your clan?

dialogue.speaker: 28CEEA184F31FFC4170D408B11ED8F8A
dialogue.line: Tell me, do you miss your home?

dialogue.speaker: B511DDCF4CA2DC1E1F43D6BED27A41B8
dialogue.line: That's... very generous of you, thank you. It should really help us.

dialogue.speaker: AF12B76C4DE9C5164509ECB1C21684AE
dialogue.line: The clan need. Must stay in mountains.

dialogue.speaker: 28D6901B4D842851EBBBBF8D56F957EC
dialogue.line: They in head. Sometime I think about clan. Mother.

dialogue.speaker: E1B26A8A4A4C8FBAD8A954968C124B7B
dialogue.line: Well, I think they couldn't have made a better choice.

dialogue.speaker: 715462234ABB067C5B286484FFFB49A5
dialogue.line: Yes, all good! Being boss is fun!

dialogue.speaker: 6795972A44FF713AA6A8BCA9CEF5593E
dialogue.line: Yes, all good! I soon become Elder! But now... come say goodbye.

dialogue.speaker: 8854C0904543C2F61E426A8750C8F474
dialogue.line: Yes. Oh, and I get coin. Really many coin. So... here. For village. To thank Coen for help.

dialogue.speaker: B7B15AEF4342B43A170BAC88886A0602
dialogue.line: You deserve! Now, I return city. Much do.

dialogue.speaker: F407BE1646847D15A80D4FB1C14008FB
dialogue.line: You visit...?

dialogue.speaker: 57B664D04F0DB9F84B2D789D43151D46
dialogue.line: Always.

dialogue.speaker: 6279158945420DB58352099961B0BDD8
dialogue.line: Anca, what is it?

dialogue.speaker: 280DCD6B459DD7E8D38807939820DDDE
dialogue.line: And I'll be here with you.

dialogue.speaker: 2DE94EFB439C5028DA3AAEBA052C431B
dialogue.line: And I'll be here with you.

dialogue.speaker: 0981E2B449850FEAFD15EE8318341ACF
dialogue.line: And I'll do my best to lend a hand.

dialogue.speaker: 347907374A58A98E642125972863D02E
dialogue.line: And Laslea can be as good a place as any to do it.

dialogue.speaker: C594B09B4274FD8747C2DFBB539A69DF
dialogue.line: And more than I ever hoped for.

dialogue.speaker: 3E946D9F43B7B4DF3E03CD9B2C024417
dialogue.line: And the new me. Someone I could maybe learn to like, one day.

dialogue.speaker: FA25A97443B969A8FB89AD9A1411668D
dialogue.line: And then I realised that was silly. What difference does it make?

dialogue.speaker: 55F81BF44BD4BB57577A768EFC3A6A0E
dialogue.line: And... The thing I asked you about?

dialogue.speaker: 83408CF44D73BE89EDAED49B09977F05
dialogue.line: Are you really fine with this?

dialogue.speaker: A56947854C5B0FD8703163B646CD5768
dialogue.line: Are you really fine with this?

dialogue.speaker: 124C06E541205C0A91B564B005C38923
dialogue.line: But I've got to admit – I was a bit cross with you for a while. We were supposed to look for the Font together.

dialogue.speaker: 3306E2AD477AC627C35801A9C04C90FC
dialogue.line: But after the Font... That urge is gone. I am where I am, and that's quite alright.

dialogue.speaker: 8596E324400261F70142D18F34D6D49D
dialogue.line: But if anyone can do the impossible... It's you.

dialogue.speaker: EF9015A446DA522235FAB38235D3BDC5
dialogue.line: But my hope is that things will be fine. The ordeal they went through... people seem to be closer than ever. Even an outsider like me can see it.

dialogue.speaker: 92B14B404657683617EA29A254A574AD
dialogue.line: But now? Is there any point to it all? To everything that's happened to me? To my family?

dialogue.speaker: E81202FD4C99C089F937D390184398A8
dialogue.line: Coen, there will always be something – bad weather, lack of money... someone needing my help.

dialogue.speaker: C026981F4B814C6A2E9F6B8EFCFCA858
dialogue.line: Coen, we've already –

dialogue.speaker: DC4D8B154F2BDE1E3922638442844DD9
dialogue.line: Coen. So, got that peat for me?

dialogue.speaker: 109E5637495A6D4AFDAC8CB73EA5E978
dialogue.line: Coen... how are you holding up?

dialogue.speaker: EBA8AE144B2E29393F987A96EEB183EE
dialogue.line: Do you have what I asked for?

dialogue.speaker: 87E6D49046917D32D83BA7A967496369
dialogue.line: Do you want me to go with you?

dialogue.speaker: 0FBB523048B91D124EC846B38ED48BBE
dialogue.line: Doesn't change how I feel.

dialogue.speaker: F75B0EC94660C3B48DB9DEAC28B8F53E
dialogue.line: Don't be. You see, I wasn't... truthful about my intentions.

dialogue.speaker: 5614BF004F272594E65E07A70B907A6B
dialogue.line: First thing in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: 79F79C704E8BF1864A0FA29814DD084F
dialogue.line: God, I'm nervous.

dialogue.speaker: 88E3AEA34CE3080305A2E3811C881117
dialogue.line: God, I'm nervous.

dialogue.speaker: 53AE469B4B7507D3FD32A3AB0576701B
dialogue.line: God, it's nice to see your face.

dialogue.speaker: F09ACCBF427344F917333BB40586B904
dialogue.line: God, it's nice to see your face.

dialogue.speaker: 32F0F53C4E77FB2515B5699F736B17C7
dialogue.line: Ha. I wish that were true.

dialogue.speaker: CB48105846852C228609DA872CB22A63
dialogue.line: Hah. It's hard to keep anything from you.

dialogue.speaker: 26CCC5F248FDA4EFECBB5B9620A5F4EF
dialogue.line: Honestly? I don't know. There are still so many questions and doubts clouding my mind.

dialogue.speaker: 8848E12345F60A1CF08CBEBFB970AD16
dialogue.line: How does it feel to be back here?

dialogue.speaker: 22A78052456281C2536A28BF88B4F90B
dialogue.line: How does it feel to be back in your old digs?

dialogue.speaker: F1616233435BEBB6A46C9DB51CE1D4F2
dialogue.line: How does it feel to be back in your old digs?

dialogue.speaker: 9A21A5C548E4424ADBE813BCED8A8932
dialogue.line: I don't know.

dialogue.speaker: 45DF36614FA894D006D34D8D7E9708E9
dialogue.line: I don't know. I'm glad it's not my choice to make.

dialogue.speaker: 6FF764BA47A917BA5433218EDE4DF107
dialogue.line: I feel lost.

dialogue.speaker: A78272DA43316B099B04498A020CE7AD
dialogue.line: I feel lost. Aimless. Fighting against the vrakhiri... it gave me focus.

dialogue.speaker: D60312F54D230BD51B9F29AFCAB6C145
dialogue.line: I feel lost. With everything that's happened... I can't just return to toiling in the fields, can I?

dialogue.speaker: 67695F10400E4A609F9E5092B82FF563
dialogue.line: I have. For now, at least.

dialogue.speaker: D46FBD0640BC59432AAE3296C4C83CE2
dialogue.line: I hope they will, Anca.

dialogue.speaker: C0CEA4E041D398E8850FC18E4DF7C8FC
dialogue.line: I hoped to use the Font myself. If the legends were true, maybe it could have given me a... a second chance.

dialogue.speaker: D19509914532A1ACB45FACBB84DD73DE
dialogue.line: I should hope so.

dialogue.speaker: 9CB8BA8F4968BB77525F1F9CC4262B7A
dialogue.line: I think I'm done with everything. Now... do you have what I asked for?

dialogue.speaker: 080EB707432FFAAC33BE4D9771C9EA9F
dialogue.line: I understand. Goodbye, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 6E7730BD49ABBD555BA70C9414B17515
dialogue.line: I wanted to say: but for how long?

dialogue.speaker: 653D52F647A3B7111E292899CFD3A61E
dialogue.line: I will always miss you. I already do. But I have to leave – before it's too late.

dialogue.speaker: B4AFD5A54EFB54AEFF8757817ABEEC16
dialogue.line: I wish I could do more.

dialogue.speaker: 8D98F1914AC2ACF813B84EBA1CAF0FD2
dialogue.line: I wish I could make you forget about all this, if only for a moment.

dialogue.speaker: 2F36264849176A918A8F54A34B7C7187
dialogue.line: I'll come back later, alright?

dialogue.speaker: 7BDCFD0546284E06280A72B0051D20DB
dialogue.line: I'll come back later.

dialogue.speaker: A14F8A0D4B6B2AFC7E68B1B2D367EEE0
dialogue.line: I'm fine. Sort of.

dialogue.speaker: D1214B03459CB505027BC097F4CA80D3
dialogue.line: I'm fine. Sort of. So much happened that it's hard to really feel anything, you know?

dialogue.speaker: C55BE85F42B000F8A582E6951DB572B4
dialogue.line: I'm not sure how to feel about... well, anything.

dialogue.speaker: 90311271471B66021CBFA384A2C97819
dialogue.line: I'm so glad you found peace.

dialogue.speaker: 247F2E6D45A4E7F16DFF23B368707854
dialogue.line: I'm so glad you've found peace.

dialogue.speaker: 0B013060462444371ADC9CAF1CA31518
dialogue.line: I'm so sorry.

dialogue.speaker: D3FCC0414D731931E31891BA525E4204
dialogue.line: If you don't have the time, just let me know. I don't want to overburden you.

dialogue.speaker: 9B3A9E30444FBB4A899542A1047A7861
dialogue.line: It doesn't matter anymore. I have to learn to play with the hand fate has dealt me.

dialogue.speaker: 7EBD54B44D65C7D25A4F7C8CC33E4205
dialogue.line: It took a while... And some help.

dialogue.speaker: 01DF88A643912285163F2995DA06D7B8
dialogue.line: It wasn't just about helping me, was it?

dialogue.speaker: B9E3BEA148A67D1323B1298DBBAE7481
dialogue.line: It wasn't just about helping me, was it?

dialogue.speaker: 2986FD9644A743A475301F9264F48A08
dialogue.line: It's a wide world out there, Coen. Full of things to be discovered.

dialogue.speaker: 784B56054CCC99A73D5F3EAE6B5F62BF
dialogue.line: It's about to snow.

dialogue.speaker: AB4828E3449EA332BB5A068EA4DD5EF7
dialogue.line: It's about to snow.

dialogue.speaker: 3B9906AF4E34A597A04FE988E6706B2E
dialogue.line: It's coming early this year, isn't it? And people are still rebuilding...

dialogue.speaker: 0346D0E949FF298337E61C8B42F3C7C5
dialogue.line: It's funny. I spent years fantasising about my life outside the valley. All the places I'd see, all the people I'd meet...

dialogue.speaker: 05F1C06A4702FEA05F1DF4BE71A73962
dialogue.line: It's not going to be easy, but they should pull through.

dialogue.speaker: 4B67440D4896ED5BA1AE6393BF9850ED
dialogue.line: It's time to stop running from the realities of my life. Can't really change it, can I?

dialogue.speaker: D813E856479C20174B44ECA7E053E958
dialogue.line: Just a word of caution: it's strong. In fact... it might prove to be lethal.

dialogue.speaker: 98B3262440F1231F19EF988F284D02FA
dialogue.line: Like any other... So yes, I guess it is.

dialogue.speaker: A850EC3B4D334F54F97CF8B56D735F14
dialogue.line: Listen, I still have some things to take care of. I'll come back later, when I'm done.

dialogue.speaker: C67F7D33408E4484F04DE88B0029BA28
dialogue.line: Made up your mind?

dialogue.speaker: E5C1DBD54AE8F5BF9C6D64A1C69E37DF
dialogue.line: Maybe because all of us have survived the vrakhiri?

dialogue.speaker: 3ADCE12A434C0E1C4BACFCACFAE9B29A
dialogue.line: My hero – keeping me warm amidst the creeping cold.

dialogue.speaker: F33230F24DB7F131F839C59E5B0C1080
dialogue.line: No more excuses.

dialogue.speaker: E2EFAD1F45D7E424111112B61CF81B32
dialogue.line: No, I don't imagine it does.

dialogue.speaker: 5C1FB0C34932F28CFEB38FBB96087F36
dialogue.line: No, no. Leave it to me. You'll have it before the day is out, I promise.

dialogue.speaker: 9ED4766C4913A594C10B61BAA8554F60
dialogue.line: No. I appreciate it but... I have to do it alone.

dialogue.speaker: 857FBDC34F100CEB5705CDAC45AC9D59
dialogue.line: Not everything will end up being as monstrous as the Font, right?

dialogue.speaker: 959195774BF9C3475543D29C7A6B8F5D
dialogue.line: Not yet, sorry.

dialogue.speaker: 31FDE67947AE614EBBF28485E1907B91
dialogue.line: Not yet, sorry. But it is on my to-do list.

dialogue.speaker: 359681AE4EAF70CB965D6B8C405F9E9D
dialogue.line: Of course, Coen. I know that... I'll wait, don't worry.

dialogue.speaker: 2972CFC64A7F6933769A12A56A584AE5
dialogue.line: Oh, Coen, you incorrigible flirt... Better tell me if you did what I asked.

dialogue.speaker: A7A3C9004202DFE1E97C56A13B3EE45C
dialogue.line: Oh, I can't imagine.

dialogue.speaker: 476D0D214B234A3521D6B097349C4423
dialogue.line: Oh? Why's that?

dialogue.speaker: B383E909455CA5B97493298C3CF5FC14
dialogue.line: Or maybe because they know that the heroic Coen of Laslea and I... well, we have this.

dialogue.speaker: FBC5826A4D807F91EB6002BE1292EB42
dialogue.line: Or maybe because they know that the heroic Coen of Laslea is my friend.

dialogue.speaker: EAF10088412D3FE9C51F0E940FE4C5E4
dialogue.line: Right. And if it doesn't work... well, I'll be here.

dialogue.speaker: 5E6A4CAE492217C80449B2A6DDF8BB45
dialogue.line: Right. And if it doesn't work... well, I'll be here. We can try something else.

dialogue.speaker: 6CCA42564FABA9F2FD620B81B1AED462
dialogue.line: Right. I live to serve.

dialogue.speaker: A8E59AB94F7E4E4A0BA2A1812F844C7C
dialogue.line: Right. I'm sorry I won't be here to help you anymore.

dialogue.speaker: 6E06E991465D62EE776DA29D8560665A
dialogue.line: Right. Listen, were you able to...

dialogue.speaker: 5478AF4640393F61770305A7A889BDCC
dialogue.line: So much has changed... And yet, so little. Always so much burden on your shoulders.

dialogue.speaker: 7587C0764D34268F1D0D75B792897C62
dialogue.line: So you made up your mind? Staying here for good?

dialogue.speaker: 8348B32D409C325D0979AE9DDB789B82
dialogue.line: So you think I shouldn't follow through with it?

dialogue.speaker: 70777C0A4608EAD8D843D9B43F370E7C
dialogue.line: So you think I shouldn't go through with it?

dialogue.speaker: 3F85E16145F0EA6C82CC179BE1E2624F
dialogue.line: So you've decided to stay?

dialogue.speaker: E2A9BA5D463E31958EEF769882130E97
dialogue.line: So you've decided to stay?

dialogue.speaker: 2D994ACC4A233A43B5979DBC6E05F8A3
dialogue.line: Sometimes you do.

dialogue.speaker: 6FD1ED214F01C0CDEBDA25B5C648297F
dialogue.line: Sorry, had to take care of a few things on the way here.

dialogue.speaker: 7D2AB93D4A6E03BCC98E9DA9B641252B
dialogue.line: Stay safe out there. Please.

dialogue.speaker: 4B591FD346DC42EE7C12C5885E4C2B71
dialogue.line: Strangely – I am. Not happy, mind you. But... accepting. Yes, that sounds about right.

dialogue.speaker: 065C896F4162F76225B53C89A854FFBD
dialogue.line: Sure, here you go.

dialogue.speaker: 3B2959F34F4A37839EA9A4A3B40D4934
dialogue.line: Sure, here you go.

dialogue.speaker: B17C63C34FCB98DC4590ECB045B530A2
dialogue.line: Sure.

dialogue.speaker: 2C081B4E437C863FD3A71AA8ED84101A
dialogue.line: Thank you for looking out for me – in spite of everything.

dialogue.speaker: FB66C8274F410AB781DBE6BF18BA3F72
dialogue.line: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: C0D63A05445183CC7A6A6AA37A2E414D
dialogue.line: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: 24130F554FA6A802F7649CB583AF4C87
dialogue.line: The only thing I'm certain of is that I'll never be free, not really. Brencis made sure of that.

dialogue.speaker: C344B0C741A981CD322561B751E1BE00
dialogue.line: The same. For many reasons. But also different.

dialogue.speaker: EE0F4202404BE038B88884B6341DEA66
dialogue.line: The villagers... they're nicer to me than they used to be. I don't really know why.

dialogue.speaker: D8B2E8B94471CECD9BC6968BC57845CC
dialogue.line: There is an... uncertainty, always looming somewhere in my mind.

dialogue.speaker: 5B10C3AE4B497F449EEB4DB2B32CFB8E
dialogue.line: There must be more to it all. Only I have no idea how to even start looking for answers.

dialogue.speaker: 94A50A8F4F1135D64C91CBAB952F63DB
dialogue.line: There you are. I was wondering when you'd show up.

dialogue.speaker: 4F83D2F044D19E0B455BC0B077A3AF7A
dialogue.line: Things got in the way. I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: 945954A041DCFC468F74459D421EC99E
dialogue.line: Things got in the way. I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: 2B2C6F9D40DBB00FE7A3D98829669139
dialogue.line: Think Laslea is ready for the winter?

dialogue.speaker: 40510122471B8B6385DA64B8BC563DE2
dialogue.line: Think Laslea is ready for the winter?

dialogue.speaker: 0D88497F4881626054C441B59598E3C7
dialogue.line: Think you'll find what you need?

dialogue.speaker: 1E16251C4CBEF7F5DC1337A2790EAC65
dialogue.line: Think you'll find what you need?

dialogue.speaker: D4EF71264437F77B8E7E2483A9367017
dialogue.line: Tonight. There's no point waiting, is there?

dialogue.speaker: 70F7F9B443E1F6E483FA1690EF6CE0B5
dialogue.line: Tough day?

dialogue.speaker: AB2C236E44231AC7F22D6781F61AE0FE
dialogue.line: Um. I've got it right here.

dialogue.speaker: B280F71F40CA3CF44191AFAC8EFFF1BC
dialogue.line: Was one of those things collecting some peat for me?

dialogue.speaker: E728C93B453F669443BD1AA7CE75EE5E
dialogue.line: When were you thinking of... of using it?

dialogue.speaker: 2831712D4DD0AB41B31990A476042107
dialogue.line: When?

dialogue.speaker: 3D433D69491CFB243F0FA997F7B6C1DC
dialogue.line: Who knows? Maybe one day we shall be reunited.

dialogue.speaker: FC0451D44496463C9E039FBDB42C8D6A
dialogue.line: Who knows? Our paths might cross again one day.

dialogue.speaker: 7B67B777497D5C065B849B9E92991DB5
dialogue.line: Wish I could go with you.

dialogue.speaker: 5E84D22D4C58E8F64B6606A264A6D671
dialogue.line: Wish we had more time.

dialogue.speaker: 5D94A6AA4137A9A4A63E89B5347D29E9
dialogue.line: With the lives we've had, what's already happened to us... No, I'm not going to worry about things I don't know.

dialogue.speaker: F42E0B1243B7B2887036B3BEEABA3AF1
dialogue.line: Yes, Coen?

dialogue.speaker: 39827FD8421C33CEE29308A5E1F39814
dialogue.line: You listen. This... this is more than I ever had.

dialogue.speaker: 7E3F025349777BA68E7FA88C3CC79620
dialogue.line: [scoff] Some happy ending I got out of all this, eh?

dialogue.speaker: CDA839F848A11D20502131A61D54A7D6
dialogue.line: ...and you got it from somewhere you shouldn't have?

dialogue.speaker: 87D5B2A142ED68A1E68358A1EAFD4B7E
dialogue.line: A man named Andrei, to be precise. A real son of a bitch.

dialogue.speaker: 8CB21C074CA7C29CE085CBBF305585A0
dialogue.line: Ah, I see. W-won't pry, then. So–so, you need something?

dialogue.speaker: BC92BB7A4C9E96DBE32B2B9B24775405
dialogue.line: Appreciate it. Now, do you want to –

dialogue.speaker: 208C0B9E49A4CD25EBC55587E23BEEB0
dialogue.line: Brought you some peat.

dialogue.speaker: 25CD12744EB7258B31AF94B6A2B4B92B
dialogue.line: But the journeyman's exam is not cheap. I needed money aaaand...

dialogue.speaker: FE47C1424A83AE066E0968A978DF423C
dialogue.line: Coen. Say, my predecessor had quite a collection here. D... did you know her well?

dialogue.speaker: ED95CB90482287DB69D86C82D17B463F
dialogue.line: Do you have what I asked for?

dialogue.speaker: 3412323A44DE218CCB5D768EDFC48E68
dialogue.line: Getting along with the villagers?

dialogue.speaker: 3EB1A43A4CA05A58C7AABA87CCA0BA34
dialogue.line: Getting along with the villagers?

dialogue.speaker: 670526984755768C001113808F344241
dialogue.line: Good to hear – wait, you're being sarcastic.

dialogue.speaker: AAF74EC040492C9980F6FF8BCA843F9D
dialogue.line: Good, good. And I have what you asked for.

dialogue.speaker: 6AFF9E55445291593C3F8DAC13E7F4F7
dialogue.line: Hello, Coen. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: 00CAC468438A8525E8C153A685ED45CE
dialogue.line: Hello, Vesel.

dialogue.speaker: 68F7B6A0478DFF2AA5648E9939F84552
dialogue.line: I feel like I should warn you – the side effects will be considerable. Potentially lethal.

dialogue.speaker: F749A6804ACB8BBEF96406A18D225FEA
dialogue.line: I understand. I'll get out of your hair now.

dialogue.speaker: 98D4156C4CDD15DB101F899090037F1A
dialogue.line: I'll come back later, if that's alright.

dialogue.speaker: C204BD4B475D05E2E40F24A2416ADB83
dialogue.line: I'll come back.

dialogue.speaker: F65C491D4CF8EA3FE33317AC888882C9
dialogue.line: I'm done with all my chores. Now... do you have what I asked for?

dialogue.speaker: D4AF0D964D9B7CAB05A971857C6CEF04
dialogue.line: Later, please. I still have some things to take care of.

dialogue.speaker: 99751E0D4E10AC07ED88BAA7F492532C
dialogue.line: Listen, I've brought you some peat. It's no firewood, but should keep you warm all the same.

dialogue.speaker: CFD1C0D54E0B640C0D021890798D5607
dialogue.line: May God protect you, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: D86108004D5CB44234128BAF1CBCFE04
dialogue.line: Me? I'm perfectly happy to keep my interactions with them to a minimum.

dialogue.speaker: F5AA717847D820C85C00FF91576287CD
dialogue.line: Of course.

dialogue.speaker: F89BC745463378D93746A5996FC0BB83
dialogue.line: So I'd say we do get along just fine.

dialogue.speaker: 4E15AFE14D61252B1CEA94A9899EF41E
dialogue.line: So for the time being I'd rather stay here, far away from people who enjoy breaking legs...

dialogue.speaker: 29EA410D4B78933B7540F2BDB5EE4F36
dialogue.line: So... Back in Svartrau, I'm still an apprentice. Should have my own shop already - what with my knowledge and skills.

dialogue.speaker: 513A566B4A0A2C47B836B8B0C88644B9
dialogue.line: Sure.

dialogue.speaker: 4FCFEE1D49D6FE1AC6D6F8A0516D1CF2
dialogue.line: Sure. Be well, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 28BA7875410E39CD90B951B6D20B0C9E
dialogue.line: Tell me – why come to Laslea? You said you wanted to collect some plants... but there must be more to it.

dialogue.speaker: 328B1D594F9C253F0671EBA8B7605286
dialogue.line: The rumour is someone got to him recently... But I'd rather stay here than test my luck.

dialogue.speaker: DCF9F57B49C0EA8B57C38782B1E39E9A
dialogue.line: They don't like strangers. To be expected, especially after what they went through.

dialogue.speaker: C805629D4028143EDD9F94B685157B5E
dialogue.line: Well, you know where to find me, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 229267E146BD8440CE51FE909E5B0040
dialogue.line: Well, you seem to be a discreet enough fellow. And a bona fide hero, too!

dialogue.speaker: E0F562E74C0724A12F2167ADEF666DC8
dialogue.line: Why come to Laslea?

dialogue.speaker: 488E437F49D2292E77D48A9078EF6A3F
dialogue.line: Yeah. She was a friend...

dialogue.speaker: 962BB7E04A687CECA8B9EA90D538A740
dialogue.line: You too, Vesel.

dialogue.speaker: 3A621D054E17B57A07662FABEF554775
dialogue.line: 'Save' is not the word I'd use. But she needn't be a mindless beast.

dialogue.speaker: 3CA695844079DA3F71B1DEBA8F7D94A0
dialogue.line: A very rare condition indeed. But one that offers... um... [chuckle] unique opportunities.

dialogue.speaker: DE8060C84BE8EB1F1B31D6ACE5465352
dialogue.line: After so many years? No wonder... Ah, it doesn't matter right now. You wanted to know about the council.

dialogue.speaker: FB9D433A4D3770FA0CB3F785DDBBA501
dialogue.line: Ah. There's a price.

dialogue.speaker: 5C6160EF46DD01AD882932A0828DEE47
dialogue.line: Alright. I will answer the Augurs's call.

dialogue.speaker: D9D2CCB64CC41EC6D9A93CBDE8422E55
dialogue.line: Alright. I will answer the Augurs's call.

dialogue.speaker: 9616EB914CECEB5D2E20D48D19FC374F
dialogue.line: Anca can't vouch for it. There's a real risk it'd do more harm than good. But there's no other way.

dialogue.speaker: 350405244853886CB64923990D882BEB
dialogue.line: And Lunka? Has she –

dialogue.speaker: 795A17E34844BBC5D1978BB014284347
dialogue.line: And an Arbiter, too.

dialogue.speaker: C3A05ABE48DD4880D04FFF87FDE7364D
dialogue.line: Anything happen while I was away?

dialogue.speaker: DF5D71E0489D03590DCD8F9DA9ADA001
dialogue.line: Arbiter? What's that?

dialogue.speaker: 44E2467F40C2B5A069A4B79B9188B1E7
dialogue.line: As a vrakhir? No, please...

dialogue.speaker: D8BC5B914E1557D34E3B3FBF6BF478C3
dialogue.line: As a vrakhir? No, please...

dialogue.speaker: 40886F98478A22B689EBCDBDE2B877F9
dialogue.line: Brencis has broken every law there is. And so, he shall be punished.

dialogue.speaker: 882764AE43CE1664C411068CB1FF0C84
dialogue.line: But she may yet thrive – in the moonlight.

dialogue.speaker: AF457B2A428A4AC29A9BE1BFB470EDAA
dialogue.line: But that's not how it works. The stronger you are, the stronger the need to put you in chains.

dialogue.speaker: B75427A64A2BF1046E06BFB5971FEE22
dialogue.line: But what about my family? I must talk to them, at least say goodbye –

dialogue.speaker: 999550944F84D051CBD0A58DD796F52F
dialogue.line: But you are a resourceful man, Coen. I can see proof of that with my very own eyes.

dialogue.speaker: 162990B64C340B98AE015283EE235087
dialogue.line: But you're not disputing my point.

dialogue.speaker: 833FD1DD49DA0D843CE0A8B8785A7E72
dialogue.line: But... There's nothing else I can do. No other remedy.

dialogue.speaker: FD5807E34347D921489F2C94ACA55446
dialogue.line: Can you do something about Lunka?

dialogue.speaker: 939254E04B6C286BB6A489B6902E2185
dialogue.line: Can you do something about Lunka? Can you save her?

dialogue.speaker: 430EE0C343322AD6F3509C9297FC9188
dialogue.line: Coen, don't do anything foolish. This man – he's very dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: E67C39D44B469EF95A636989F2870402
dialogue.line: Commendable.

dialogue.speaker: B75EBED64B07B7B444FF17AA8F5D2A32
dialogue.line: Don't mind me, Coen. This time, he's the one you want to focus on.

dialogue.speaker: 48C61E83409020AB2FE7158B03C5CCDC
dialogue.line: Eternity is an awfully long time to walk this Earth aimlessly, drifting.

dialogue.speaker: 2B0B692B4FF9C87768A583A3B22F4E5F
dialogue.line: Ghhhhahhhh.....

dialogue.speaker: 717FF9FF474AA2A0001000AA330E61EB
dialogue.line: Ghhhhahhhh.....

dialogue.speaker: B6E73DC84C7B5BF4C70FC5A775419092
dialogue.line: Ghhhhrrr....

dialogue.speaker: 8AD91EE94FBE89BB3FBFB5A5F663A8D4
dialogue.line: Hey, sweet pea. I brought you a few things.

dialogue.speaker: D239A2ED441AFAC1A0871AAE16B204F4
dialogue.line: I also brought the concoction.

dialogue.speaker: DAA589474644D6B176B4B0A3BB8F8A40
dialogue.line: I also brought the potion from Anca's.

dialogue.speaker: 99714BE9499E5A7E100DCA9945142365
dialogue.line: I also brought the potion from Vesel's.

dialogue.speaker: 9927A4324F90D9AF5832AEBAD703C329
dialogue.line: I came here to see to that... Only to learn that someone else rose to the task.

dialogue.speaker: 4216058C42E6D6DF87E8AD849C701635
dialogue.line: I can't lose her, too. Can't fail again.

dialogue.speaker: 038F37584C3718B792B524AE52F8B4D4
dialogue.line: I have no intention to harm any of you. In fact, I came here to help you, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: AD7A1CBB4053F5FD1271C0AB611D2A79
dialogue.line: I have the potion.

dialogue.speaker: EDD32B9D4FF887600B4A39BB2EB0B3B8
dialogue.line: I have the potion.

dialogue.speaker: 5B7226E344A1B3B3AC736C8E8B1B9F33
dialogue.line: I hope you will find purpose in our calling. I know I have.

dialogue.speaker: AE01DCBF4FFDA90879F4769C5B8789BD
dialogue.line: I imagine getting the components needed to forge it was quite a challenge, yes?

dialogue.speaker: 237AF3F24C9AFB31FEA057977092F1A6
dialogue.line: I thought you'd be pleased.

dialogue.speaker: 870C05C146AC42EA271358A1711E4CF0
dialogue.line: I want to say goodbye to my family.

dialogue.speaker: E54F5E3344E8B82427DBD39B05FCFE5D
dialogue.line: I'd rather say 'entrust you with a mission'.

dialogue.speaker: 3CC6E3C64F3093FB0AFF7EB457492C8C
dialogue.line: I'm sorry, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 535A5233445BDA9D5B036C9B4BC9C6D3
dialogue.line: I'm sorry, Coen. If you want to save your sister, you must leave Vale Sangora at once.

dialogue.speaker: 25ED425C41753AD7C6D53AB04B7E7774
dialogue.line: I... I was afraid you'd say that. But... if there's no other way, so be it.

dialogue.speaker: 16EBCBC444A7B5F7198A9CAB131FE53E
dialogue.line: If there's no other way...

dialogue.speaker: 0817E3BA459B5A07BC70CBB6B5617D45
dialogue.line: If you do nothing, she'll remain a feral beast. One that can only be... put down.

dialogue.speaker: A8E7DCED42EEF3E2FECA1796D75624BB
dialogue.line: Indeed. I hope it helped. Although now I can admit that it was a test, too.

dialogue.speaker: B28413B241C6E4C52DBF00B5D3D2C393
dialogue.line: It is vital you leave right now. Soon, the snow will block the passes – and your sister cannot wait.

dialogue.speaker: A7C53F1D49F48CE2EB04EDA47D768E45
dialogue.line: It means that when Brencis tried to change you into a vrakhir, something went wrong.

dialogue.speaker: ED185C05482924FE8FA804A99B6FBD47
dialogue.line: It shall be neither easy nor quick... But in time, no one shall remember his name.

dialogue.speaker: ED2C93294A7D971E607C9B9FA6AEC4C2
dialogue.line: It shall be neither easy nor quick... But in time, no one shall remember his name.

dialogue.speaker: ED87D3514854D1ED7659F2BCD5AF45DB
dialogue.line: It shall be neither easy nor quick... But in time, no one shall remember his name.

dialogue.speaker: 65126BB64C1400FC4C574BBB63D19893
dialogue.line: It's all my fault.

dialogue.speaker: 8D736657400015315E7F869BC7E96109
dialogue.line: It's all my fault. I let it happen again, like with Alin.

dialogue.speaker: 29F83965456F686E3102AFB22D3E9F47
dialogue.line: Just as I helped you before by letting you know how to obtain the armour you're wearing.

dialogue.speaker: 40EE3F8E4B85548DAFF837A7BA3C2516
dialogue.line: Lacra - say something.

dialogue.speaker: E364F258476E62403375B5A143889D7F
dialogue.line: Lacra – say something.

dialogue.speaker: 181AF1AB49A7AF9E1F0411A5FEEC64D5
dialogue.line: Lacra? What are you –

dialogue.speaker: CC10831D48F265CCAE368E9F7997B9DD
dialogue.line: Lacra? What's going on?

dialogue.speaker: 04DCF84D4C243BA95396C796DEBD8595
dialogue.line: Luckily, you're mistaken.

dialogue.speaker: 191B06A04C2B16485EC469BFFDD2F9B8
dialogue.line: Luckily, you're mistaken.

dialogue.speaker: C56ABE4C41E16F7D6E98C8BF10F924FE
dialogue.line: Lunka, I'm so sorry.

dialogue.speaker: C5802B014495FFB229AA6F89DF97072A
dialogue.line: Lunka... I'm so sorry. I should have been there to protect you.

dialogue.speaker: EF2343904437C50F12C5B8867B4963F4
dialogue.line: Mihai mentioned the Augurs...

dialogue.speaker: D68411CE4E596C04CFD703ACCFF524DD
dialogue.line: Mihai? So he's alive?

dialogue.speaker: 09434A36433B32D28F13198FE6AAF1DF
dialogue.line: My name is Neberu. We haven't met – I arrived in Vale Sangora only recently.

dialogue.speaker: B9B4E88246890FFF9393B695D8C3D1FC
dialogue.line: My name is Neberu. We haven't met – I arrived in Vale Sangora only recently.

dialogue.speaker: 3D03FE78476FE8DEAA6369A13B2A66B0
dialogue.line: Neberu? Why are you here?

dialogue.speaker: 55E60B9F4AED3F3E3F93148E0A774850
dialogue.line: Neberu? Why are you here?

dialogue.speaker: 8028D5BF424B939C69566FB94A7A020A
dialogue.line: Neberu? Why are you here?

dialogue.speaker: C50A24894390CB34FAFE578ADF664E9F
dialogue.line: Neberu? Why are you here?

dialogue.speaker: A030D78E42F497CAAADE649573009D87
dialogue.line: No. I still have to clean up the mess made by Brencis and his lackeys.

dialogue.speaker: 3F85FEA04747648359CE20874F8868CD
dialogue.line: No. I'm a dawnwalker, just like you.

dialogue.speaker: 78B76A2C4CCFE3158D31238A0F298E34
dialogue.line: No. Someone still has to take care of Brencis.

dialogue.speaker: 11087079409800AB915133BA7F04F1CD
dialogue.line: Not to mention persuading the blacksmith to actually work on it...

dialogue.speaker: 082649704EF49556384842B52636FCB3
dialogue.line: Nothing of note. A group of hunters was roaming the woods nearby, but I scared them off.

dialogue.speaker: 2587B1894786BD3FA436029E6CE73393
dialogue.line: Now you are stuck between night and day.

dialogue.speaker: 6342782745A4BA4E75AF4FB0BEFD0A5F
dialogue.line: Oh, God...

dialogue.speaker: 6DBA33BF48A30AC0DC59BF8E77DCC913
dialogue.line: Oh, I've been following your actions for a while. The armour schematics I sent you proved useful, no?

dialogue.speaker: C868165D4F1C0B52CCCCD291764FDE3B
dialogue.line: Oh, you needn't worry. If there's one thing I'm good at, it's keeping secrets.

dialogue.speaker: 9F0BC36342313E2E0C4E13A3B4514699
dialogue.line: Only... It might not work. It might make things worse.

dialogue.speaker: D64A121B4601F8EF70780A80F4FA05D2
dialogue.line: Please, friend. Don't do this to yourself.

dialogue.speaker: EC018C6D4F4EB45FC4775999B1F866BE
dialogue.line: Please, say something...

dialogue.speaker: A5A8BA914E2D610081D33FB279BC2AC4
dialogue.line: So I'd be selling my soul.

dialogue.speaker: 477761C844538E9608F3B7AA9A831BD8
dialogue.line: So that's why I change back into a human when the sun rises...

dialogue.speaker: 579E42C8496E35DBEA8A2DA3CAAA16E4
dialogue.line: Someone who solves problems. Such as Vale Sangora.

dialogue.speaker: BF85DCBE4C7B5966D315A490D6CFE9D7
dialogue.line: Sounds like you want to use me.

dialogue.speaker: 79293FD04B93555E7178F68651FB904F
dialogue.line: Tell me what to do.

dialogue.speaker: 6D10A55D4A37537ED488D5A390DDAA98
dialogue.line: That was you? But... Why?

dialogue.speaker: EDA389094E888004F70CC2A71589ECFE
dialogue.line: That's not how it works, I'm afraid.

dialogue.speaker: BECB5A1F4370C663121D5488A84E0709
dialogue.line: The Augurs – they want to make you an offer. And you musn't refuse.

dialogue.speaker: 7D84CB4E4DA9964572931D8595EAFAB6
dialogue.line: The Augurs... Mihai mentioned them to me.

dialogue.speaker: F9A5BABB4E39242B1B9F73A768462744
dialogue.line: The Council of Augurs sent me here with a different task in mind... But I believe I can help you, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 35407F464EF138F76CED3DBABBE9D4C7
dialogue.line: The Council? What council?

dialogue.speaker: EE8C1A6F4AF63FB362B3A08F924ED696
dialogue.line: The Council? What council?

dialogue.speaker: E88E6CF041B3EFBE107CAA9616EF78F1
dialogue.line: There always is.

dialogue.speaker: 2E991A7B43A0B07894E89B962126FF35
dialogue.line: There is not much to be said, Coen.

dialogue.speaker: 979CF19647C888C6A23955B25ECF7561
dialogue.line: There's little the Augurs cannot do... And little they will not ask for in return.

dialogue.speaker: 0D3D302F4FFD8C11153675A2A0BF32A3
dialogue.line: There's no time.

dialogue.speaker: 61787A1E4A039C8FAEC9CE9FE5E38581
dialogue.line: They are my... superiors. Suffice it to say, they do not appreciate Brencis's claim of power.

dialogue.speaker: 1CADC3E3447F9DF4D4913082EBB4A439
dialogue.line: This child deserves a second chance. You know what to do, my friend.

dialogue.speaker: FF863CCE47B95024CC2DB7BE645351F4
dialogue.line: This is the only way.

dialogue.speaker: 84C91E714E4C7DE1B1B4EAAF98282BC0
dialogue.line: This should keep you warm. And.... and I brought you something to eat.

dialogue.speaker: 46654E13449AE9EBB0D28583428DEAB4
dialogue.line: True. But... She's your sister.

dialogue.speaker: 7F11147F4485667670D3389F55B090DD
dialogue.line: Very well. Here, take this letter and follow its instructions.

dialogue.speaker: BAADDB574799B9CA99143AA5E954FC53
dialogue.line: Vesel can't vouch for it. There's a real risk it'd do more harm than good. But there's no other way.

dialogue.speaker: 9F7BD24446B154EBB49781B192F793A3
dialogue.line: Vicho, the Council of Augurs appreciates your decision to play no role in Brencis's madness.

dialogue.speaker: 0C50E057401229DED8088C93B5E41D23
dialogue.line: Vicho, what do you think?

dialogue.speaker: C32336154A75A0DDAB04A8961069DFF5
dialogue.line: Vicho, what do you think?

dialogue.speaker: 7A42BADD459E1AA5B5EE12A0918E5733
dialogue.line: Wait, it was you who sent me that letter?

dialogue.speaker: 6D50F3494A4B4B492514B0ACE96C9616
dialogue.line: Wait, you're not coming with me?

dialogue.speaker: C22C807549B5EDECAFFB9FAFCB0E4ECE
dialogue.line: Wait, you're not coming with me?

dialogue.speaker: E5D043AB4581B9BFB70152A6B04E32BD
dialogue.line: Was. There was nothing I could do to save him.

dialogue.speaker: 30AD3BBD4EF69DD0D870A9BAD6DDAF2E
dialogue.line: We all have something we'd sacrifice everything for.

dialogue.speaker: 3C36C1B74F74022B69E71EBCA6775C0A
dialogue.line: We cannot return her stolen humanity.

dialogue.speaker: 63B48B72443DB9C58EC732BEA5A70C19
dialogue.line: We will meet again, Coen of Laslea.

dialogue.speaker: A345C7224E2B7CFC98F9738530AC6E2B
dialogue.line: We will meet again, Coen of Laslea.

dialogue.speaker: E1C17F7D44F1111437732493EB01E1BD
dialogue.line: We will meet again, Coen of Laslea.

dialogue.speaker: 1ECCED724D2C763305AA76B2A9ABE777
dialogue.line: What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: 7319FF9C440C61B778E609AD3AFBC0ED
dialogue.line: What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: FA4672A2402DFE1BEAF9D6AC59B26AEA
dialogue.line: What's a dawnwalker?

dialogue.speaker: D91A31E44E5C1084D0CE9CB623CE5D95
dialogue.line: What's an Arbiter?

dialogue.speaker: 0F511CCB4282B9489088A3AB3A6AF6AE
dialogue.line: Who the hell are you?

dialogue.speaker: 1CA402DC40FA5F3C625F7396863FEC54
dialogue.line: Who the hell are you?

dialogue.speaker: 628399E840EA34201D1A72B4D0C9BC0D
dialogue.line: Who the hell are you?

dialogue.speaker: E7A271504BC9DA6A73FD3EB290B4D67F
dialogue.line: Who the hell are you?

dialogue.speaker: FBCCEA9940A643CF810D3AB0ADCD84CE
dialogue.line: Why are you so interested in me?

dialogue.speaker: 906EAEAB43D08BBF27E1F1A32A78C591
dialogue.line: Why so interested in me, I wonder?

dialogue.speaker: 4DC4301B4BEBED36F159B28C2DDDC9E9
dialogue.line: You barely even know me and –

dialogue.speaker: 864C3BF74515241A4E5DAF903DC6DD10
dialogue.line: You can't tell anyone about my sister – what you saw here. Understood?

dialogue.speaker: 1AE1895447C95E9DFEE6D78562C218D0
dialogue.line: You can't tell anyone about my sister.

dialogue.speaker: AF552088445A28D12B85048DEE0CAA06
dialogue.line: You know I hate what I've become. And yet, even so...

dialogue.speaker: 911601C44C32E8732F4A4284C3357204
dialogue.line: You might've thought your powers would grant you independence. That no one would tell you what to do now.

dialogue.speaker: 9CFE3D3F44663CD554FF3492A74EA88D
dialogue.line: You say you're a dawnwalker. And apparently I am one, too. What... what does that mean?

dialogue.speaker: 0FC11F9A4A4610AF8A27E6AD8CF99057
dialogue.line: You sent me that letter?

dialogue.speaker: CA5A2ACF43FFEA8C24A7E5B0B8FCDC7D
dialogue.line: You wear them, too? You, of all people?

dialogue.speaker: 0C54972E4E422EC1234D7FA53D8C708D
dialogue.line: You're a rarity, Coen. And a precious one at that.

dialogue.speaker: 6BA628ED495239ADAA4139806716CAFC
dialogue.line: You're... You're not human.

dialogue.speaker: 0F7A9A92485ED1658901B7B80D7A0FC3
dialogue.line: Anca was restless. Looking for ways to undo the past - to cheat Death itself.

dialogue.speaker: 75863F5449E266D57B996596F372BA3F
dialogue.line: Anca... I'm glad she let go, came to terms with her past.

dialogue.speaker: 1633EB16455564728A7322863F9764B1
dialogue.line: Anca... It just wasn't meant to last, what we had. Alas.

dialogue.speaker: 514EACEC4FFB3DFC725D62859FC59F45
dialogue.line: Anca... It just wasn't meant to last, what we had. Alas.

dialogue.speaker: 7C3D1D344BCC29EAA0D5059EEDE107E6
dialogue.line: Crossing the mountains in the winter... Few took that risk. Then again, few were as determined as she was.

dialogue.speaker: C499512C4B8B12889ABBB6AFF1C2CBE9
dialogue.line: Hard, cold winter. One of many to come.

dialogue.speaker: E2FA101F407D007809D9C8805F8EED90
dialogue.line: She didn't take much. Just some clothes, dried food... And books, of course.

dialogue.speaker: 984862A642A49C18503DB0B2E9C3BD28
dialogue.line: She was so full of regrets...

dialogue.speaker: E053C0374EF1130335B10B83C7A2CFB4
dialogue.line: The monsters retreated into the shadows... But didn't disappear.

dialogue.speaker: 3AF9861640558F34F5710BB2BE5FD793
dialogue.line: The priests never liked women like her. Then again, she knew how to take care of herself.

dialogue.speaker: 102A48A6423A28DFC7EDA4BC75305723
dialogue.line: The villagers – they took her in, finally. Accepted her for who she was.

dialogue.speaker: 366B8961408E0ABE427F45B3C4D0E573
dialogue.line: Where did she mean to go? What beacon was she following? Part of me wants to know... Another wishes never to.

dialogue.speaker: 42AEFA954B52F8635F943489BE90543A
dialogue.line: Where her winding path took her... I do not know.

dialogue.speaker: 1C287C1C4DA0A6FF4EAF98A0C51C2CA4
dialogue.line: And, for a while at least, feel as if nothing's changed.

dialogue.speaker: 0861B0EC49FA2F5E4EC434AB6552362E
dialogue.line: As tempting as the whispers from the shadows are, I have managed to resist them... For now.

dialogue.speaker: D56B48E14640CDD0902BC388B898304F
dialogue.line: Early in my life as a dawnwalker, I felt unmoored, drifting. But not for much longer.

dialogue.speaker: 6AB39D154F9755BC5553739B3BD516C3
dialogue.line: Every night I change. Crave blood. Struggle against the darkness filling me from within.

dialogue.speaker: 669F17184F68383212994E9696E0A66B
dialogue.line: I feel like I should miss my old life, long for my lost humanity. But I don't.

dialogue.speaker: 65E640044F4A606E0D7E6EB80DEC1359
dialogue.line: I have been watched, and closely so. My future – all but determined.

dialogue.speaker: A343C53C47A3A007EA7C6DA1B256044B
dialogue.line: I may no longer be human, but I strive to act as one.

dialogue.speaker: AF9ACE844085890430335CAB7F8AE193
dialogue.line: I smile with each nightfall, bask in the moon's cold light. I know what the darkness brings - and I welcome it.

dialogue.speaker: 20A4431A452964327647CAA041E6EFEE
dialogue.line: I was afraid, at first. Of the night, of what I'd become, what I craved. But now? I've learned to embrace it.

dialogue.speaker: 81DD59E64B65DA1565876E93EC930349
dialogue.line: I'd like to think I'm still me. That whatever's been implanted inside me hasn't yet seeped through to my soul.

dialogue.speaker: 8D7AE0E541B3CE49641F07B6FC5EE1C2
dialogue.line: I'd like to think I'm still me. That whatever's been implanted inside me hasn't yet seeped through to my soul. But for how much longer?

dialogue.speaker: 0BDD9FE74CF99C33B042BEBCCDC4491A
dialogue.line: I've changed, yes. The darkness lodged within me? Let it bloom, let it spread, feed on the blood I drink.

dialogue.speaker: 9264D0F848A29BB5784D25BCE6D419D9
dialogue.line: If there's one thing I'm grateful for, it's that I can still enjoy the sun's warm touch on my skin.

dialogue.speaker: 94676C744C427994B84400A7AF126DB7
dialogue.line: It requires constant focus... And slipping could be fatal.

dialogue.speaker: 826B07BF469BDEAD0239EE800EAE208F
dialogue.line: Straddling the line between the night and day – finding a balance between the two - is a delicate act, one akin to rope-walking.

dialogue.speaker: EC7F948A4070DC3D6EC22BBB533DFE37
dialogue.line: And each night, as they shuttered their windows and went to bed, the nuns's singing carried over the forest...

dialogue.speaker: EFBF74914DC8CA6E514D60835A322766
dialogue.line: And so, the fog grew thicker and thicker... Until it started spreading beyond the convent's walls.

dialogue.speaker: 2E4E1A4C4CCA047F491DFE8B06E09138
dialogue.line: Anyone who interrupts them, however... Is dealt with swiftly.

dialogue.speaker: 534F686C4E692FE87352ADB0CC21C64E
dialogue.line: Even though the convent was no longer haunted, the locals gave it a wide berth. Soon, its walls were overgrown with ivy, and the bones turned to dust.

dialogue.speaker: 6A8BF0BC43197B3E0BA8408BD784190F
dialogue.line: Freed from their neverending chores, they didn't simply collapse or turn to dust – instead, they spread over the local mountains and forests, stumbling aimlessly...

dialogue.speaker: AC05E46843F19A67C8911995FF243427
dialogue.line: Glimmering, maddening lights light up the night skies. And, worst of all, the dead rise from their graves...

dialogue.speaker: 4CA66FC145AB9F8843C0799D8A0E183F
dialogue.line: I didn't let Anca finish the ritual Leonica started. There were too many unknowns, too many risks.

dialogue.speaker: 5317F1DF485570AE71125F811D872AD5
dialogue.line: The fog spreads, and with it – unnatural and unsettling events. Swarms of moths destroy pastures and orchards.

dialogue.speaker: 4F86386A4636A4B04D49F5A250A4D746
dialogue.line: The fog, which once covered the convent like a thick shroud, lifted, revealing empty ruins.

dialogue.speaker: FF01E4BE4B5C1EF4A3FFB1BE2B7B18C6
dialogue.line: The locals knew not to approach the convent's walls.

dialogue.speaker: AD4D7FCA483AA452E0AB2897868A6819
dialogue.line: The nuns no longer roamed within its walls... But they weren't gone, either.

dialogue.speaker: 9D4BD95B48017C5E945E5FB061EC1DFA
dialogue.line: The unfortunate nuns, neither alive nor entirely dead, still perform their duties, tirelessly and meticuluously.

dialogue.speaker: 037F3348493BDC5A218EC6B4C3214725
dialogue.line: Until someone crossed their path, that is.

dialogue.speaker: A2B250514DEDA9F47E5A6A89F9D95BC6
dialogue.line: As for Lunka... My fate was intertwined with hers. For all eternity.

dialogue.speaker: BB0793B1401D86EBA3A99C8403379E92
dialogue.line: I realise now I don't know much about my father. Yet I miss him to this day.

dialogue.speaker: DDFA308741C027AE149B69846980685B
dialogue.line: I saved my family... Or what was left of them. My father was left to look after my siblings alone.

dialogue.speaker: 6F5D3F13407A4EC3879B81A412722C82
dialogue.line: Mirto... As stubborn as he was brave. I wonder what kind of man he grew up to be. Whether he remembered me.

dialogue.speaker: 016AD09D4C5B14F8190F1FB46F57115B
dialogue.line: My family home. Empty, deserted. Because I failed.

dialogue.speaker: 1E56C1BE4E15F042C52543A1F0538940
dialogue.line: My family – they survived, lived on. Whether happily or not... I cannot tell. We were to never meet again.

dialogue.speaker: D5C4ED3A45CC3D705072188443BFA8BC
dialogue.line: My mother got better – for a few days, I witnessed it myself. I treasure every word she said, every time she met my eyes.

dialogue.speaker: 447B0ECB453D541A6972F9A92766F3D7
dialogue.line: Only Lunka survived... To suffer for all eternity.

dialogue.speaker: EF47898F4563ADE5062093BF8C4F3630
dialogue.line: Whether he lived up to the task, I do not know. We were to never meet again.

dialogue.speaker: AC6F4C5F4360D9CD940FF992BC963EB1
dialogue.line: Yanna. Ever the responsible one. I hope she started a family of her own. I hope it was happier than ours.

dialogue.speaker: 6947BF1A46C8BA6BF77198B2D0A44947
dialogue.line: After Florin's death, the Church canonised him – he's patron saint of the virtuous. A stinging irony.

dialogue.speaker: 042CA2754F1DA129793AAAB5290C4B7D
dialogue.line: And the catacombs? Sealed and buried under seven feet of rubble.

dialogue.speaker: 2A155C47403F6828AAE82FBBD4F1DFC9
dialogue.line: As soon as Brencis was dethroned, most of Father Florin's flock turned against him - and those still loyal to the priest couldn't protect him.

dialogue.speaker: 9966C1CA4D04D7810691CB935C34C954
dialogue.line: Brencis needed to find another priest willing to blaspheme, lie, and manipulate. It proved very easy.

dialogue.speaker: 97CD11EC4F3FCD0C59F048A8AA1635F8
dialogue.line: Catalin disposed of Florin... And quickly found another priest willing to justify the cruelest excesses of Vale Sangora's sire.

dialogue.speaker: F2857703415DE528FB394CAEFC0100B2
dialogue.line: Disturbing, bloody rituals continued to be performed inside Svartrau Cathedral for years to come.

dialogue.speaker: 45F316354FBF6E678BA0009D87E13592
dialogue.line: Even today, its crumbling ruins seem infused with unspeakable evil.

dialogue.speaker: 8381B3184C6DAE5157D9C9876BCD0A5B
dialogue.line: Evil men rarely get what they deserve. I'm glad Florin was an exception.

dialogue.speaker: 6BCF1C434D7259F0B13C64B3EE97E8DA
dialogue.line: Father Florin always enjoyed being the centre of attention.

dialogue.speaker: 2FDB9D53498F181E134C3CA7C8235FC5
dialogue.line: Father Florin... Or should I rather say, Saint Florin of Sangora? With my help, he managed to erase the memory of his sins.

dialogue.speaker: DAF48C504B36C0D923A794945F3DB6BA
dialogue.line: Few of his flock took objection to that decision.

dialogue.speaker: D281804842F516A92EEEF5B4D66D7B31
dialogue.line: Having learned of Florin's betrayal, Brencis showed little mercy. He was so offended he even refused to drink the fallen priest's blood.

dialogue.speaker: 981694AB44AC096276AB8F80546C8456
dialogue.line: It'd be easier to catch a greased pig than to get that man to own up to his mistakes.

dialogue.speaker: ACFE9EE6439EA6F88C1307B792D32267
dialogue.line: One of the first orders Catalin issued as the newly installed knyaz of Vale Sangora was to burn Florin at the stake.

dialogue.speaker: F9DDFE9F4B394932131D70903B2AC1DC
dialogue.line: People need hope and consolation. Give them that, and they'll forgive you for anything.

dialogue.speaker: FDE46AFF45B83A1F939629AA6DDC8F91
dialogue.line: St. Mihai's Cathedral was ritually cleansed, all signs of the blasphemous cult washed away.

dialogue.speaker: 6887A14547738590F186CFA83D37581F
dialogue.line: Turns out lambs can be bloodthirsty, too.

dialogue.speaker: 8C41FBD945B3028064A1AABB6C253E38
dialogue.line: And, for their sanity's sake, it should stay that way.

dialogue.speaker: 40362CF648A67E5A2B4199B08B0776B4
dialogue.line: Erratic and excitable, kobolds are hard to reason with. Still, I did my best to part with them on peaceful terms.

dialogue.speaker: D186C6CC4CC5566F10A298A18FD9AC3B
dialogue.line: First glance, kobolds seem as stupid as they are treacherous. But I've learnt they have some semblance of a culture, too.

dialogue.speaker: EE8E3B7A4F04D3541FEE8E88CFF3531D
dialogue.line: I might drink blood, but I don't enjoy spilling it unnecessarily.

dialogue.speaker: 8BE34EC148F63FD43C82BAB9533121D6
dialogue.line: Never travel alone in the Carpathians. And if you do, stay clear of any caves, crevices or gorges.

dialogue.speaker: 8760D6C142C6D19D1F1021918B6B5CB6
dialogue.line: One that values unity... And gorging on rotting meat.

dialogue.speaker: 0DB8EBBF4E10A98EDCDEFA8A13492B4B
dialogue.line: So much is hidden from the eyes of simple folk. Little do they know what watches them from the shadows, what slumbers far below.

dialogue.speaker: 636578BB43D658EE3FD218BFECF97694
dialogue.line: Such prime property attracted other, potentially even more dangerous beings...

dialogue.speaker: 5A0F214F475EDBDECC4469A5131E4978
dialogue.line: The kobolds's paintings were all they left behind, destined to puzzle explorers for centuries to come...

dialogue.speaker: F0028F2244944093994942BC267A783A
dialogue.line: They emerge from their hideouts only rarely, to snatch a wayward sheep... Or a shepherd.

dialogue.speaker: D91EA2F44522D134F0FFBAB59F625FF6
dialogue.line: To my best understanding, kobolds live in the caves beneath Vale Sangora to this day.

dialogue.speaker: 2224ABD84C02364B1EFAE9A6D2E8AB56
dialogue.line: Together with Lacra, I slayed every last one of the treacherous kobolds of the Rockfalls range. But their caves weren't empty for long.

dialogue.speaker: 434A55A24A148094BD38B3B44829B3EB
dialogue.line: After I defeated Brencis – without her help, and so to her great annoyance – she swiftly moved on to other business, travelled to other lands.

dialogue.speaker: 3DE71D534B867FD78B7C6DBE587CDE7B
dialogue.line: Alas, vrakhiri can hope for no such thing.

dialogue.speaker: 335E25EB426C5D01E43A7BBCE8E8EDD1
dialogue.line: Always on the run from someone, always outwitting her pursuers. Lacra didn't mind the constant danger – she revelled in it.

dialogue.speaker: 435038914920A702B2B2B0B820952717
dialogue.line: By sentencing Lacra to death, I saved Brencis’s prisoners. Was it worth it? How do we tell if one life can ever be worth more than many? I keep asking myself these questions every night.

dialogue.speaker: 5F8FA7F44C4B99C94A90A4B60DC965D7
dialogue.line: Do vrakhiri have souls? Of sorts. Empty husks, devoid of any last traces of humanity, driven solely by the lust for blood – and hate.

dialogue.speaker: 0ECDDF26484CF5C2B0A78F9B9E1C60F9
dialogue.line: I often wonder – what is that thing? What does it want? When will I hear its maddening voice next?

dialogue.speaker: C8D8C95C43267C42B18CBC8797028F7F
dialogue.line: I wonder where her journeys took her next? To the sun-scorched steppes of Asia? Or Africa's lush rainforests? One can only guess...

dialogue.speaker: 5F9752D44A7CD283AD7F9A8C1D3B215F
dialogue.line: I wouldn't wish this fate on my worst enemy – much less a lover.

dialogue.speaker: 2282A83C43FB16490C4B73837C6DCBBB
dialogue.line: Lacra did not linger in Vale Sangora.

dialogue.speaker: B4740DE4493D9441322379A30CC28A01
dialogue.line: Lacra did not linger in Vale Sangora. Having defeated Brencis with my help, she swiftly moved on to other tasks, travelled to other places.

dialogue.speaker: 030BF3014A066FC5170E08A77FAE9962
dialogue.line: Lacra died as she lived – driven, determined, unflinching. I wish I could tell you these virtues were rewarded in the afterlife that awaited her.

dialogue.speaker: A0ECE4F243D53BCC10EDEF8D4882CABE
dialogue.line: Lacra was arrogant enough to think she could take Brencis and his clique on her own, without my help.

dialogue.speaker: 88D18DF34260EE1377BFB08363D08A75
dialogue.line: Lacra was my first guide. She taught me what I needed to know, helped me when I needed assistance.

dialogue.speaker: FE72ED1E4ABB7C358F2772ADCE3304BB
dialogue.line: Lacra was my first guide. She taught me what I needed to know, helped me when I needed assistance.

dialogue.speaker: D0BC6B334E39867A45582A9DD115E942
dialogue.line: My goal was simple – to save my family. I was willing to go to extreme lengths to achieve it... And make costly sacrifices, too.

dialogue.speaker: C120D39B4767057FC3F9F689CAE8D8C2
dialogue.line: On whose orders? Why? I was to learn the answers to these questions soon, maybe even sooner than I had wished.

dialogue.speaker: F86BB12F44EB20537D467BB6A73DBC37
dialogue.line: On whose orders? Why? I would soon learn the answers to these questions, maybe even sooner than I had wished.

dialogue.speaker: EEC00522429055050270CD93E7557A58
dialogue.line: Reluctantly and resentfully, of course - but, I'm still grateful to her.

dialogue.speaker: 3B9462114788830A46D3F6B791331889
dialogue.line: She died a painful death... And that was just the beginning of her suffering.

dialogue.speaker: 8C5F91824FC6542087684EAF8A785E93
dialogue.line: She'll wander the cursed plains of Anachora for centuries, gradually losing her sense of self... And then join the likhos.

dialogue.speaker: E67D380445DD473CAF9CB3BE02111381
dialogue.line: She'll wander the cursed plains of Anachora for centuries, gradually losing her sense of self... And then join the likhos.

dialogue.speaker: 22415B4E46B7E327F94332B14700546E
dialogue.line: Unwillingly and resentfully at first... But she grew fond of me as time went by.

dialogue.speaker: 6A4B0F654BDCAED8536B24A29F4A2929
dialogue.line: Wherever she went, Lacra brought destruction in her wake. But how do you fight fire, if not with fire?

dialogue.speaker: EDBA7C3947442F581E02DDBCCC9A0C5E
dialogue.line: And if their wages were even a day late, they'd happily pillage what they were meant to protect.

dialogue.speaker: B544EFEC4135EE63EAA1E38D600286F8
dialogue.line: Any rebellion is dangerous... And a rebellion against the vrakhiri doubly so. Without my help, the manumits did not outlast Brencis.

dialogue.speaker: 6A54D1714CC20CAF42715F87BC642671
dialogue.line: But Marat and the manumits were there to greet them.

dialogue.speaker: 8BB912154F821280C72322BCF30F955F
dialogue.line: But as it turned out, few of them would die of old age...

dialogue.speaker: AD04F9C34D58A69DEC97619F4E00FC3F
dialogue.line: Catalin didn't trust his own subjects and composed his army of foreign mercenaries. They didn't care much for Vale Sangora...

dialogue.speaker: E18565234BDC324BC6939896B9969704
dialogue.line: Catalin was determined to stamp out all monsters from the valley. And, with Marat's help, he succeeded.

dialogue.speaker: 6C0F93D34E118BD9EE7D0DB151B56079
dialogue.line: Even though we didn't always see eye-to-eye about what was best for the valley.

dialogue.speaker: C9A0208E4478DDE501E764BF397FD837
dialogue.line: I saved Brencis’s prisoners by sentencing the rebels to death. Was it worth it? How can we tell which lives to spare and which to sacrifice? I keep asking myself these questions every night.

dialogue.speaker: 5577F90E4827C52F443F5CA1BC8ADBF5
dialogue.line: Marat and I shared a goal and I grew to respect him. But we never became truly close... I'm not sure he even wanted any friends.

dialogue.speaker: EA5EFEDA4A35268C69281DA5C19CDAD0
dialogue.line: Marat got what he wanted – he became Catalin's right hand man. And as such, he enforced his policies with ruthless efficiency...

dialogue.speaker: 6184358D440C52B93505A98F5B30D471
dialogue.line: Marat took up his sword to fight against monsters. But as soon as they were gone, he learned that humans could be just as cruel and bloodthirsty.

dialogue.speaker: F5CEBD374C5A96BE5626DC955B4091C7
dialogue.line: Marat trusted me, against the advice of his comrades. I wonder whether, in his dying moments, he realised what a huge mistake he'd made.

dialogue.speaker: FD9875B841C639C937411894C68D1042
dialogue.line: Marat was determined and ruthless. Unfortunately for him, so was Brencis.

dialogue.speaker: 455D4390425BF3CA10ABF482C75561D5
dialogue.line: My goal was simple – save my family. I was willing to go to extreme lengths to achieve it... And make costly sacrifices, too.

dialogue.speaker: EF0C3B2E455D151104E32281A86C8C77
dialogue.line: Nature abhors a vacuum. As soon as word got out that Svartrau Castle was standing empty, all sorts of brigands and ruffians crossed the mountains to ransack the sireless valley.

dialogue.speaker: 813B867B482D784ED625DBB27E0F0956
dialogue.line: Nothing brings you closer than facing mortal danger together. Marat and I became good friends...

dialogue.speaker: 4994086240DCD33071B800A9118A0972
dialogue.line: Nothing brings you closer than facing mortal danger together. Marat and I became good friends...

dialogue.speaker: F37A054A47A6178748EE2C81EAFC4EB3
dialogue.line: The manumits hoped that, with Brencis gone, they could go back to their old lives, hang up their weapons and leave them to gather dust.

dialogue.speaker: 3FCDCAB94623908530AD9BA3CBE7E777
dialogue.line: The manumits were the last spark of opposition Brencis had to contend with... And with my help, he extinguished it once and for all.

dialogue.speaker: DDC6625D450CE6A9C5509F8ED6027B7F
dialogue.line: Then, briefly, something more. What we had wasn't meant to last.

dialogue.speaker: 3508A26B42703D0CC0BB5EBFA4145A39
dialogue.line: Today, no one would believe the uriashi lived high up among the Carpathian peaks.

dialogue.speaker: 346B5EDE49BFBA754C3720AD593FC2E8
dialogue.line: Vrakhiri need blood to survive... Humans just enjoy watching it get spilt.

dialogue.speaker: 146839D04C65BEBC7BFD67B03B9A7863
dialogue.line: A few dared to oppose her... only to end up in the gutter.

dialogue.speaker: F50C5B5C4DA8CCEC9FCD2FAC67AB2905
dialogue.line: A monster for a boss? As long as the money was right, Svartrau's underworld didn't mind.

dialogue.speaker: 976ADE9144CC235036707189BDC7D888
dialogue.line: Always curious, always hungry for more... I'd never met anyone who'd enjoyed life more than her.

dialogue.speaker: D780CA3A4EE4FF281E523392EC843C3D
dialogue.line: Even in the hardest of times, unscrupulous men found ways to turn a profit. Ocha made sure they shared their takings.

dialogue.speaker: 7E4367ED4E822A7E99650C8287CA56AA
dialogue.line: Every operation needs brawn – and brains.

dialogue.speaker: 498C566A43DB1932C2BA998D5FD9AF3A
dialogue.line: I wonder, how far did Ocha's wanderlust take her? All the way to Portugal's rocky coast – or even further?

dialogue.speaker: 7330C03B47235C3A093136AE9B9542E2
dialogue.line: Ironic, isn't it? That Nora would feel safe only when accompanied by a monster...

dialogue.speaker: 883FB54646AF46401C01DB892183B12F
dialogue.line: Ocha couldn't stay in Svartrau but wouldn't return to her clan. What happened to her? I don't know for sure, although... There were rumours of a giant horned woman in Croatia and Slovenia, making ribald jokes and wrecking inns...

dialogue.speaker: AA8793A64550D5FBBA4AC9B327124AD9
dialogue.line: Ocha filled Andrei's shoes – but found them several sizes too small. With Nora's help, she expanded the original operation.

dialogue.speaker: 94E45E9044C141BFA4F52DBFE01FB3C2
dialogue.line: Ocha grew to be a respected matriarch. She kept her village safe for centuries to come... Though privately, she missed the bustle of human cities.

dialogue.speaker: 8750C27A4204C84076FD559915C1885B
dialogue.line: Ocha had no qualms about her line of work. 'Me strong, they not,' she'd say with a shrug.

dialogue.speaker: 3E08D99C44DE6F05A40B2CB71B41887E
dialogue.line: Ocha respected uriashi traditions... But sometimes changed them, too. Her experience in Svartrau taught her that in order to survive, one has to adapt.

dialogue.speaker: CA2A321948F09B6E72B8AB830C9555EF
dialogue.line: Ocha understood humans like no other uriash. And that's exactly why she made sure none was ever admitted into her lands.

dialogue.speaker: 9E8518DE42DE47718C0430ABDAC6CC72
dialogue.line: The whole valley knew to stay clear of the rugged peaks of Rockfalls. Rockslides came down those slopes with unnerving frequency...

dialogue.speaker: B61EE8B743E9925BCBE5B080A9265D41
dialogue.line: The world of humans was like a magnet to her. Sometimes it pulls... And sometimes pushes away.

dialogue.speaker: C07C13904248AE74847D44A7145E0CC2
dialogue.line: Uriashi don't need much: a cave to live in, some moss to nibble on. If they were greedier, like us... the world could be a very different place.

dialogue.speaker: 3B7277694C4CB82CC8E214A792F64689
dialogue.line: Brencis continued to rule over Vale Sangora for years... And yet, history books never mention his name, as if his rule had been erased from memory. By whose hands? Ah, that's a tale for a different time.

dialogue.speaker: 148C549949AF949D5D0540B18C8D1D9B
dialogue.line: Brencis was gone... But so was Catalin. With his death, Vale Sangora faced an uncertain future.

dialogue.speaker: F75A076E457A032CBE51429071CF094F
dialogue.line: Brencis was gone... With no one to replace him. Vale Sangora faced an uncertain future.

dialogue.speaker: 62F76698434768E4C621CFA31B991F8C
dialogue.line: Catalin showed no mercy to those who had supported the vrakhiri. Whole districts were burned to the ground.

dialogue.speaker: 95AEF5C74C0576580B3E3C8F0152D446
dialogue.line: For years to come, people told stories of a valiant hero who stormed the castle singlehanded and slayed the evil knyaz.

dialogue.speaker: 3612F2D349941DB5450D699D4BED93E7
dialogue.line: In the end, they became legends – told and re-told, but given little credence.

dialogue.speaker: A700886D4F2E16E24603C89F2DDABA26
dialogue.line: In the end, they became legends – told and re-told, but given little credence.

dialogue.speaker: 3AE2024D447BB40CA9763E87B794591E
dialogue.line: Its walls were decorated with murals showing a monstrous being emerging from stormy clouds... Just a myth? Or something more?

dialogue.speaker: 2FEDC1AB4D34B4793FF6DFA7B4EFBB06
dialogue.line: Life in Svartrau carried on as before. Its inhabitants were well-fed, safe from the plague... And bled every Sunday.

dialogue.speaker: D07FF558421EEBE944248B9FC178351F
dialogue.line: Most villages continued to pay the blood tithes... But not all: Laslea was exempt. Brencis may have been a monster, but he kept his promises.

dialogue.speaker: 612A00EF464BCE2029463195D3B610A1
dialogue.line: Only an occasional rockslide, aimed at a nosy shepherd, reminded the people of Vale Sangora of their existence...

dialogue.speaker: F633569D4544DC5CEC9D8DAB218CA3D9
dialogue.line: People got used to the monsters living among them - and they, too, became more brazen, unafraid to step out into the sun. But it was not meant to last...

dialogue.speaker: F0592C3A4F5D7945157B4595E9322B93
dialogue.line: People told stories of blasphemous rituals conducted in the castle's dungeons: of chanting in forgotten tongues, of swarms of crimson-coloured moths.

dialogue.speaker: 6034CBDF4E1DAC61CF86378FE193DAF8
dialogue.line: Soon, armies crossed over the mountains and blood flowed freely.

dialogue.speaker: 925A6654471E742C48037B98A31514B3
dialogue.line: Soon, bands of ruffians prowled the streets, eager to pick a fight, and Svartrau's cobblestones were slick with blood.

dialogue.speaker: A85D46CB4E97E890539D1D966F422D6F
dialogue.line: Stories of bloody rituals and people ripped to shreds by an invisible force circulated for years.

dialogue.speaker: 1A909CFB46AB89D63EF082AEC148C468
dialogue.line: The blasphemous images of vrakhiri and their gods were removed – never to be mentioned again.

dialogue.speaker: 1F20259749E5D3CF30BBB1A4ECCA3994
dialogue.line: The castle stood empty – free for the taking. Once the plague subsided, neighbouring rulers's minds turned to Vale Sangora and its silver.

dialogue.speaker: 8116342643411B45993E158A2B5FEA76
dialogue.line: The city cathedral was remodelled in keeping with Brencis's wishes.

dialogue.speaker: 41A6E60E40F3D6671018C69206BB4E14
dialogue.line: The uriashi retreated to their villages, high among the peaks, never to be seen again.

dialogue.speaker: 0CB72F9D4F74EA4BBDF5CD9B74A492C9
dialogue.line: The young knyaz spared no expense in rebuilding the castle. And its dungeons were as crowded as ever.

dialogue.speaker: 308A7EE64210FE2D9BBE98AB8F151094
dialogue.line: Whether they were made up, or contained a grain of truth, I do not know...

dialogue.speaker: F79ED43C40947577D04B1BA4AE6D0BC0
dialogue.line: With Catalin's return, the old order was restored, built on the sacrifice of the Manumits. A shame Marat never got to see it...

dialogue.speaker: 6EBEA34A475B1825576315A1104F0920
dialogue.line: With Catalin's return, the old order was restored... For better or for worse.

dialogue.speaker: 3FF4D93840A77185177A37A133DF6979
dialogue.line: With no one to pay for its upkeep, the city guard disbanded.

dialogue.speaker: F9A5F51B43C65D3DC4DFFB8B3275829A
dialogue.line: Without the vrakhiri blood, the plague soon returned to Vale Sangora. A steep price to pay for regaining our dignity...

dialogue.speaker: C80436F64862504B44609E984109C09A
dialogue.line: But I convinced him there was still hope to make amends – and maybe even gain redemption?

dialogue.speaker: A91EAF60454E108BBBEECFAA038EC5DE
dialogue.line: Could it have been...?

dialogue.speaker: 79394C47429BECA0F1F851B195C06A34
dialogue.line: Few suspected Vicho's true nature. The townspeople knew him as a kind, gentle man... Who aged very well.

dialogue.speaker: ED1B11A74A97D6F7FBB0478A03884B93
dialogue.line: He realised a vrakhir couldn't go without blood altogether... So instead, he started consuming it in moderation.

dialogue.speaker: 0F79D5B24571158BE579AC97D3EAD013
dialogue.line: I was convinced I'd solved the murders of Vicho's friends, but I was wrong – and more people died as a result.

dialogue.speaker: 00167450498A7ED8790543903A990E24
dialogue.line: I'm glad he finally found peace. Few things are harder for a vrakhir.

dialogue.speaker: C046F6F343863F4CF22D6281790B4400
dialogue.line: More sorrow, more misery...

dialogue.speaker: E2A83E3C491E8C4C9E288CBF4228C9FC
dialogue.line: No human did this. They were murdered by someone who craved blood – and lots of it.

dialogue.speaker: 4E0816414792AC0DD9A5DF827B2FC30D
dialogue.line: The city guard could never solve a case like this one. And even if they found the culprit... He'd cut them down in a blink.

dialogue.speaker: D3C9E2CF40D23D105932DBB963D15541
dialogue.line: Vicho tried his best to make up for his many sins. It'll take a long time. But then - he is immortal.

dialogue.speaker: B8EAFE8042B37738E2B267B59A8800C4
dialogue.line: When Vicho learned he was the one behind the deaths of his friends, he was devastated, ready to end his own life.

dialogue.speaker: 0A4AB0B24CD36A5EC4355C9813DBEC76
dialogue.line: And those who set out to find them always get lost in a thick fog...

dialogue.speaker: D250FDE34C45C8DF7FAA219376B57267
dialogue.line: But her love for her daughter was as strong as it was on the day she was turned.

dialogue.speaker: C7F357CB41D67ECB65CE3D9FF498FF2E
dialogue.line: How old was Xanthe? I don't truly know. Old enough for the darkness within her to twist her body and drown out her own thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: D84BF1B949CD8A19823CCC80902D3A4B
dialogue.line: I spared Xanthe and her daughter. I still wonder why. Was it only to gain an ally in my fight with Brencis...

dialogue.speaker: B682A87648EFAFD183C0D9A9FEA1F77D
dialogue.line: Or did I, on some level, feel sorry for those two?

dialogue.speaker: 71C19B8D4C5BDBDEF033928682E845FC
dialogue.line: Poor girl. A broken body, a tortured mind. I hope someone puts her out of her misery one day... But I'm glad it wasn't me.

dialogue.speaker: 5616E4494EE681CCB54EBE81C2C0DF3A
dialogue.line: She didn't notice that the girl's mind was unravelling – or didn't want to notice.

dialogue.speaker: 878019F24D8839E0859AF1B70E188CB8
dialogue.line: Wherever Xanthe and her daughter go, young women disappear without a trace.

dialogue.speaker: 7FB32218488D1DFB009ABE925F53CDB9
dialogue.line: Xanthe kept thinking of Chariklea as her child, to be protected, entertained, coddled.

dialogue.speaker: DDB4E41145E64AB545F6289862045706
dialogue.line: Don't worry, it will be ready soon. You can focus on other things for now.

dialogue.speaker: 989B983D4A0A9FF1320B04AD9A56BDA7
dialogue.line: I still need a bit of time. Go, take care of your other errands.

dialogue.speaker: 397FBF474C4E92536FD791A04E418844
dialogue.line: Shouldn't rush these things, Coen. Go, I need some space.

dialogue.speaker: EF02C6DD443A57A59D9361A5080713F4
dialogue.line: Good morrow to you.

dialogue.speaker: 725DBEA648A74E8B27BDF3BE0AD5C9B4
dialogue.line: Honey from Tantari! Best in Vale Sangora!

dialogue.speaker: 7F9399F34AE1E5F89F0DAAA51489B03D
dialogue.line: Honey! Honey for sale!

dialogue.speaker: F19081A84B781DA5E0B21B9DFEFE0D37
dialogue.line: And now we're able to bring God's word back to this church. Yes, it does feel a bit unreal.

dialogue.speaker: BAD8ABBC47727D7C302AC0874F392E73
